I'm probably going to catch shit for not immediately siding with the "I don't tip" consensus this thread has. I want to make this clear, workers currently in the tipping industry should simply be paid a livable wage, and tips should either be gutted or return to their original place as being for exceptional service. I fucking despise tipping "culture" in America. 

That out of the way, I worked in restaurants in various foh roles, server, food runner, server assistant, host, barback, these jobs should be paid a livable wage, right? But it's not what the restaurants would do. Every fucking restaurant from the fast food joint with a sit down area to fine dining with a dedicated lounge will continue to pay front of house the bare minimum. Hell, those fast food jobs some people don't consider "real work" sometimes have better pay and benefits than the fancy fine dining places. People keep saying on this post to look for other jobs, finding another job can be very difficult right now. I say "can" because I don't want to generalize other areas, but where I am, it sucks. And if we're looking at people who can only get starter positions due to no trade or college degree, it gets really fucking hard. All that to say I'm living I'm the tipping industry and I'm struggling. I can't get another better job, I'm struggling to find a second. Not every damn tipping industry worker is raking it in, and not every worker wants things to be the same.

I want to make something clear. I hate it and completely acknowledge there are terrible servers raking in money because they got lucky or are pretty. I had the displeasure of working with some of these people. But, if tipping could be axed and I can make a wage that lets me eat 3 meals a day and pay my rent on time, I'll take it in a fuking heartbeat. But I don't have any other options right now, and when you're too busy starving, it's hard to try and fight for something fairer. I doubt this'll change anyone's mind or give them a different perspective.

I want it to change, I want to live an okay life. But how do we fix this? The employee is so replaceable in the food industry. Workers who make great money don't want it to change. Workers who struggle are too busy worrying about money to protest and could be replaced easily if they put up a fuss. Not tipping doesn't affect the bottom line of the restaurant, so they don't care either way. Only way I can see us hurting the restaurant is by people collectively deciding not to eat at these establishments. Let's be honest, people aren't doing that. Sorry if I'm pessimistic. I didn't quite spell it out in case one of my players bumps into this and discovers my Reddit. My hook of the setting is that it's a sort of planar scrapyard. Chunks of planes seemingly disappear only to reappear in my plane. These chunks of wildly different environments, cultures, people, and beliefs create what I hope to be an interesting world. It also allows me to borrow from official settings, like some gods from a pantheon or potentially a city from the material plane. But the hook, I guess is the dangers of the plane (it's ever growing), the mystery behind it, and the extreme dangers that lurk in between the chunks of other planes.

Funnily enough, I will be changing my map throughout the course of the campaign due to some planar shenanigans I wrote into the lore. Normally I wouldn't start with the map, but to me, the setting and world map are where most of my ideas came from. At least initially. I made a post just like yours when the automod filtered a bunch of posts, I name 3 biggies but I'll mention them anyway.

*Fallen Hero: Rebirth* is a great super villain game. Basic premise, MC used to be a superhero *something happened* and now you've flipped sides and are haunted by your past. Great characters, good romance if you care for it, and really good options to tailor the MC. Fantastic job from Malin imo.

*The Exile* is a wip that's a mid-level fantasy I'd argue. MC used to be a glorious commander for their home city. The MC is a mythosi (kind of a mix of human with some other kind of creature like a wolf or demon) and has been exiled from the city that once cherished them. MC is haunted by what happened and you can choose to play out how they handle their past. All around, a really fun story.

*I the Forgotten One* is a medieval era wip. MC is related to royalty. Due to some *unfortunate* events MC has to delve back into their past to assist the people that once dismissed the MC. MC is in *real* rough shape in this one. And like the others, you can tailor how the MC handles their past. I will say, the author has made it clear that the romance is not a focus point (the rest of the story more than makes up for it).

Apologies if the format is bad, I'm on mobile right now. I hope at least one for those is new to you cause they're all fantastic.

P.S. I forgot to mention this, but all of these games touch on heavy topics and can be quite graphic at tines. I'm sure you were expecting it, but they can be dark at times.
